people.name: Abraham Lincoln
people.why: Held the country together through civil war and ended slavery; assassinated five days after it ended.

people.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
people.why: Led the movement that dismantled legal segregation, and made non-violent protest a global template.

people.name: Louis Armstrong
people.why: Turned jazz from ensemble music into an art of the individual soloist, and changed all popular music after him.

people.name: Toni Morrison
people.why: Nobel laureate whose work put Black American interior life at the centre of the literature.

people.name: Thomas Edison
people.why: 1,093 patents, and the industrial research lab itself may have been his most consequential invention.

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.what: Thirteen colonies broke from Britain on a claim of universal rights that the country has been arguing over ever since.

events.title: The Civil War
events.what: Around 700,000 died over slavery and secession — still the deadliest war in American history.

events.title: The Great Depression
events.what: Economic collapse reshaped the role of government through the New Deal.

events.title: The Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts
events.what: Ended legal segregation and disenfranchisement after a decade of mass protest.

events.title: Apollo 11
events.what: Humans walked on the moon, watched live by roughly a fifth of the people alive.

culture.label: Regionalism
culture.text: The South, New England, the Midwest, Texas and California are as different as separate countries in food, speech and politics.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: American football on Sundays in autumn, baseball in summer, basketball everywhere. College sport is close to professional in scale.

culture.label: Thanksgiving
culture.text: The biggest travel weekend of the year, and for many families more important than Christmas.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Friendly and informal fast — first names immediately, and small talk with strangers is normal, not intrusive.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Barbecue, Tex-Mex, soul food, Cajun, New York pizza: the regional cuisines are the real ones.

talkAbout: Where they're from — the state and city matter enormously.
Sport, especially their college or hometown team.
Road trips and national parks, which almost everyone has opinions about.
avoid: Politics, guns, religion and healthcare are all live and polarised. Race is discussed but not casually with strangers.

people.name: Terry Fox
people.why: Ran across Canada on one leg to raise money for cancer research; the annual run is now global.

people.name: Frederick Banting
people.why: Co-discovered insulin and sold the patent for a dollar so it would stay cheap.

people.name: Leonard Cohen
people.why: 'Hallelujah' alone has been recorded hundreds of times; he was a serious poet first.

people.name: Wayne Gretzky
people.why: Holds so many records that his assists alone would make him the highest scorer in NHL history.

people.name: Viola Desmond
people.why: Refused to leave a whites-only cinema seat in 1946; she is now on the ten-dollar note.

events.title: Confederation
events.what: Four colonies joined to form the Dominion of Canada, adding provinces over the next 82 years.

events.title: Vimy Ridge
events.what: Canadian divisions took a position that had defeated others; often described as the country's coming of age.

events.title: Patriation and the Charter
events.what: Canada took full control of its constitution and adopted the Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

events.title: Truth and Reconciliation
events.what: The commission on residential schools documented what was done to Indigenous children and called it cultural genocide.

culture.label: Hockey
culture.text: Ice hockey is the shared reference point, from frozen ponds to Saturday night broadcasts.

culture.label: Bilingualism
culture.text: English and French are both official; Quebec's distinctiveness shapes federal politics constantly.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Poutine from Quebec, butter tarts, Nanaimo bars, and maple syrup taken seriously enough to have a strategic reserve.

culture.label: First Nations
culture.text: More than 600 First Nations, plus Inuit and Métis peoples, with land and treaty rights central to current politics.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: The politeness is real but is also a running joke Canadians make about themselves.

talkAbout: Which province they're from, and the rivalry with the one next door.
Hockey, and how their team is doing.
Winter, and their strategies for surviving it.
avoid: Don't assume Canada is a version of the United States — it's the fastest way to annoy someone. Residential schools and Quebec sovereignty are serious subjects.

people.name: Frida Kahlo
people.why: Turned her own pain and identity into the most recognisable body of self-portraits in modern art.

people.name: Benito Juárez
people.why: A Zapotec shepherd who became president, separated church and state, and defeated a French emperor.

people.name: Octavio Paz
people.why: The Labyrinth of Solitude is still the book Mexicans argue with about their own identity; Nobel 1990.

people.name: Diego Rivera
people.why: Put Mexican history on public walls at enormous scale and made muralism a political movement.

people.name: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
people.why: A nun who out-argued the bishops on women's right to learn, three centuries early.

events.title: Tenochtitlan founded
events.what: The Mexica built a city on a lake island that became one of the largest in the world; Mexico City sits on it.

events.title: The fall of Tenochtitlan
events.what: Cortés and his Indigenous allies took the Aztec capital, beginning three centuries of colonial rule.

events.title: El Grito de Dolores
events.what: Father Hidalgo's call to arms began the independence war; it's re-enacted every 15 September.

events.title: The Revolution
events.what: Zapata, Villa and a decade of civil war produced land reform and the 1917 constitution.

culture.label: Día de Muertos
culture.text: Families build altars and spend the night at graves — a celebration of the dead, not a mourning of them.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Corn, chilli and beans across thirty regional cuisines; Mexican cooking is UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Family
culture.text: Extended family is the default social unit, and Sunday lunch is close to obligatory.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Mariachi from Jalisco, banda from Sinaloa, son jarocho from Veracruz — regional and fiercely defended.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: 68 Indigenous languages are recognised; Nahuatl gave English chocolate, tomato and avocado.

talkAbout: Food, and which region does which dish properly.
Día de Muertos and how their family observes it.
Football, and the Liga MX club they support.
avoid: Cartel violence and migration are exhausting subjects for many. Don't mistake Día de Muertos for Halloween, and don't do the sombrero-and-siesta routine.

people.name: José Martí
people.why: Cuba's national hero, claimed by every faction; 'Guantanamera' uses his verses.

people.name: Fidel Castro
people.why: Led the 1959 revolution and ruled for nearly half a century.

people.name: Celia Cruz
people.why: The Queen of Salsa, whose voice defined Cuban music abroad after she left in 1960.

people.name: Alicia Alonso
people.why: Danced Giselle while nearly blind and built one of the world's great ballet companies in Havana.

people.name: Compay Segundo
people.why: Buena Vista Social Club made him famous worldwide at 90.

events.title: The Spanish-American War
events.what: Spain lost Cuba; the United States occupied it and kept a base at Guantánamo.

events.title: The Revolution
events.what: Castro's forces overthrew Batista, and Cuba became the first socialist state in the Americas.

events.title: The Missile Crisis
events.what: Thirteen days that took the world closer to nuclear war than at any other point.

events.title: The Special Period
events.what: The Soviet collapse cut Cuba's economy by a third; the improvisation of those years still marks daily life.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Son, rumba, mambo, cha-cha-chá and salsa all come from here; music is everywhere and mostly live.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: Baseball, argued about daily in Havana's Parque Central by an informal debating club called la esquina caliente.

culture.label: Improvisation
culture.text: 1950s American cars kept running with Soviet parts — resolver, making do, is a national skill and a national joke.

culture.label: Medicine
culture.text: Cuba trains more doctors per head than almost anywhere and sends medical brigades abroad.

culture.label: Food and drink
culture.text: Ropa vieja, moros y cristianos, and rum in a daiquiri or mojito.

talkAbout: Music and dance — the fastest way into any conversation.
Baseball, and the Havana teams — it is argued about daily in the street.
Family abroad; almost everyone has relatives in Miami or Madrid.
avoid: Politics is risky for Cubans to discuss openly with strangers, and the embargo and the diaspora split opinion sharply. Let them steer.

people.name: Rigoberta Menchú
people.why: K'iche' Maya campaigner who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992 for indigenous rights.

people.name: Miguel Ángel Asturias
people.why: Nobel laureate whose Mr President is the archetypal Latin American dictator novel.

people.name: Jacobo Árbenz
people.why: His land reform was ended by a CIA-backed coup in 1954, which set off decades of war.

people.name: Carlos Mérida
people.why: Fused Maya motifs with European modernism across murals in Guatemala and Mexico.

people.name: Ricardo Arjona
people.why: One of the best-selling Latin American artists of the last thirty years.

events.title: The Maya classic period
events.what: Tikal and its rivals built cities, astronomy and a full writing system in the Petén rainforest.

events.title: The coup
events.what: A CIA-backed operation removed the elected president after his land reform threatened United Fruit.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: 200,000 killed, mostly Maya civilians; a UN commission found the state committed genocide.

events.title: The peace accords
events.what: Ended the longest civil war in Central America.

culture.label: Textiles
culture.text: Each Maya town has its own huipil pattern — you can read where a woman is from in what she wears.

culture.label: Volcanoes
culture.text: Thirty-seven volcanoes; Fuego erupts almost continuously and Antigua sits in their shadow.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Pepián, a thick spiced stew, and tortillas made fresh at every meal.

culture.label: Semana Santa
culture.text: Antigua's Holy Week processions walk over vast carpets of dyed sawdust made overnight.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: 22 Maya languages plus Xinka and Garífuna; roughly 40% of the country is Indigenous.

talkAbout: Textiles, and how to read the patterns.
Lake Atitlán and the volcanoes.
Coffee, which is among the best in the region.
avoid: The civil war and the genocide against Maya communities are recent and unresolved. Don't romanticise 'Maya ruins' to people whose living culture they are.

people.name: Óscar Arias
people.why: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987 for the plan that ended Central America's wars.

people.name: José Figueres Ferrer
people.why: Abolished the army in 1948 and put the money into schools and health.

people.name: Franklin Chang Díaz
people.why: Flew seven Space Shuttle missions, a joint record, and develops plasma rockets.

people.name: Carmen Lyra
people.why: Her Stories of My Aunt Panchita are the country's best-loved folk tales.

people.name: Keylor Navas
people.why: Won three consecutive Champions League titles in goal for Real Madrid.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Central America broke from Spain; news reportedly took a month to reach Costa Rica.

events.title: Abolishing the army
events.what: After a short civil war, Figueres dissolved the military — Costa Rica has had none since.

events.title: The Arias peace plan
events.what: Brought the region's civil wars to the negotiating table and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: Running on renewables
events.what: Costa Rica generated over 98% of its electricity from renewable sources for a fifth straight year.

culture.label: Pura vida
culture.text: Greeting, farewell, thanks and outlook all in two words. It is used constantly and meant sincerely.

culture.label: Nature
culture.text: About 5% of the world's known species on 0.03% of its land, with a quarter of the country protected.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Coffee built the country's middle class in the nineteenth century and is still a matter of pride.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Gallo pinto — rice and beans — for breakfast, and a casado plate at lunch.

culture.label: No army
culture.text: No military for over 75 years; the anniversary is a public holiday.

talkAbout: Pura vida, and what it actually means to them.
Wildlife and national parks.
Coffee, and the region it comes from.
avoid: Ticos dislike being lumped in with their neighbours' conflicts. Nicaraguan immigration is a touchy domestic subject.

people.name: Rubén Blades
people.why: Made salsa political with 'Pedro Navaja', then ran for president and served as a minister.

people.name: Omar Torrijos
people.why: Negotiated the treaty that returned the Canal to Panama.

people.name: Roberto Durán
people.why: World champion at four weights and one of the greatest lightweights in the sport's history.

people.name: Mariano Rivera
people.why: The first player unanimously elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame.

people.name: Rosa Guerrero de Chiari
people.why: A pioneer of women's education and civic participation in Panama.

events.title: Separation from Colombia
events.what: Panama became independent with United States backing, and immediately granted canal rights.

events.title: The Canal opens
events.what: One of the largest engineering projects ever attempted, at the cost of tens of thousands of workers' lives.

events.title: Martyrs' Day
events.what: Students were killed protesting over the flag in the Canal Zone; it became the turning point toward handover.

events.title: The handover
events.what: Panama took full control of the Canal at noon on the last day of the century.

culture.label: The Canal
culture.text: About 3% of world trade passes through; the handover is a defining point of national pride.

culture.label: Molas
culture.text: The Guna people's reverse-appliqué panels are among the most striking textile art in the Americas.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Salsa, típico accordion music, and a strong Caribbean reggae en español scene.

culture.label: Panama City
culture.text: A skyline of towers next to a 17th-century old town, both on the Pacific.

culture.label: Crossroads
culture.text: Canal workers came from the Caribbean, China, India and Europe, and the country reflects all of it.

talkAbout: The Canal, the expansion, and what the handover meant.
Baseball and boxing.
The Guna Yala islands and mola textiles.
avoid: The 1989 US invasion and the Noriega years are sensitive. 'Panama Papers' jokes are wearing thin.

people.name: Bob Marley
people.why: Made reggae a global language and remains one of the most recognised figures on earth.

people.name: Marcus Garvey
people.why: Built the largest Black mass movement in history and shaped Pan-Africanism and Rastafari.

people.name: Usain Bolt
people.why: Eight Olympic golds and world records that still stand — the fastest human ever timed.

people.name: Nanny of the Maroons
people.why: Led escaped enslaved people against the British and is Jamaica's only national heroine.

people.name: Louise Bennett-Coverley
people.why: Made Jamaican Patois respectable as a literary language.

events.title: England takes Jamaica
events.what: Spain lost the island; enslaved people who escaped into the mountains became the Maroons.

events.title: The Baptist War
events.what: Sam Sharpe's rebellion of 60,000 enslaved people hastened Britain's abolition of slavery three years later.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Jamaica left British rule and immediately became a cultural power far beyond its size.

events.title: The One Love Peace Concert
events.what: Marley brought the leaders of two warring parties on stage and joined their hands.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Ska, rocksteady, reggae, dub and dancehall all came from one island in about twenty years.

culture.label: Sprinting
culture.text: A country of under three million dominates world sprinting; Champs, the school athletics meet, fills a stadium.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Jerk seasoning was developed by the Maroons; ackee and saltfish is the national dish.

culture.label: Patois
culture.text: Jamaican Patois is a language in its own right, and its rhythm has travelled worldwide.

culture.label: Rastafari
culture.text: A faith and movement born in 1930s Jamaica, with real theology behind the imagery.

talkAbout: Music, and which era of it they rate.
Athletics, especially around Champs and the Olympics.
Food, and where to get the best jerk.
avoid: Rastafari isn't a lifestyle accessory, and weed clichés get old. Crime statistics and colonial nostalgia both land badly.

people.name: Francisco Morazán
people.why: The last president of the Federal Republic of Central America and the great champion of regional union.

people.name: Berta Cáceres
people.why: Lenca leader who stopped a major dam and won the Goldman Prize; murdered a year later.

people.name: Ramón Amaya Amador
people.why: Prison Green exposed conditions on the banana plantations and became the national novel.

people.name: Lempira
people.why: Led resistance to the Spanish; the currency is named after him.

people.name: David Suazo
people.why: Honduras's most successful export to European football, at Cagliari and Inter Milan.

events.title: Copán
events.what: A Maya city whose hieroglyphic stairway is the longest Maya text known.

events.title: The banana republic
events.what: United Fruit and its rivals came to control land, railways and governments — the phrase was coined here.

events.title: Hurricane Mitch
events.what: Killed around 7,000 people and set the country's development back by decades.

events.title: The coup
events.what: President Zelaya was removed by the military, beginning a long political crisis.

culture.label: Copán
culture.text: The finest Maya sculpture anywhere, in a valley near the Guatemalan border.

culture.label: Garífuna
culture.text: The Caribbean coast's Garífuna people have their own language, punta music and UNESCO-listed culture.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Baleadas — a thick flour tortilla with beans, cream and cheese — are eaten at any hour.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: Football, and a 1969 World Cup qualifier with El Salvador that helped trigger a short war.

culture.label: Reef
culture.text: Roatán sits on the second-largest barrier reef in the world.

talkAbout: Copán and the Maya past.
Baleadas, and where the best ones are.
The Bay Islands and diving.
avoid: Migration, gangs and the 2009 coup are all politically charged. 'Banana republic' as a joke is not funny here.

people.name: Rubén Darío
people.why: Founded modernismo and reshaped poetry in Spanish; Nicaragua calls itself his country.

people.name: Augusto César Sandino
people.why: Fought the US occupation for six years; the Sandinistas took his name.

people.name: Ernesto Cardenal
people.why: Liberation theologian, revolutionary minister of culture, and one of the great Latin American poets.

people.name: Gioconda Belli
people.why: Her poetry and memoirs of the revolution are read across the Spanish-speaking world.

people.name: Alexis Argüello
people.why: World champion at three weights and one of the finest technicians the sport has seen.

events.title: William Walker
events.what: An American filibuster seized the country and made himself president before being driven out.

events.title: US occupation
events.what: American marines occupied Nicaragua for two decades, opposed throughout by Sandino.

events.title: The Sandinista revolution
events.what: The Somoza dynasty fell after 43 years; a literacy campaign followed within a year.

events.title: The Contra war
events.what: A US-backed insurgency fought the Sandinista government through the decade.

culture.label: Volcanoes
culture.text: Nineteen of them; Cerro Negro is young enough that people sledge down it.

culture.label: Poetry
culture.text: Nicaragua genuinely calls itself a nation of poets, and means it.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Gallo pinto, nacatamal wrapped in banana leaf, and vigorón on a plantain leaf.

culture.label: Lake Nicaragua
culture.text: The largest lake in Central America, with its own population of freshwater bull sharks.

culture.label: Güegüense
culture.text: A satirical colonial-era dance-drama, UNESCO-listed, that mocks the Spanish authorities.

talkAbout: Rubén Darío and poetry.
Volcano hiking and Ometepe island.
Baseball, which is more popular here than football.
avoid: Current politics is genuinely dangerous to discuss for many Nicaraguans, and the 2018 protests and their repression are raw.

people.name: Óscar Romero
people.why: Shot at the altar for denouncing state killings; canonised in 2018.

people.name: Roque Dalton
people.why: The country's greatest poet, killed by his own guerrilla faction at 39.

people.name: Claudia Lars
people.why: One of Central America's most admired lyric poets.

people.name: Salvador Salazar Arrué
people.why: Cuentos de Barro captured rural Salvadoran speech and life as nothing had before.

people.name: Prudencia Ayala
people.why: Ran for president in 1930, before women could even vote, and forced the question into the open.

events.title: La Matanza
events.what: A peasant uprising was crushed with the killing of tens of thousands, most of them Indigenous Pipil.

events.title: Romero assassinated
events.what: The archbishop was shot saying mass the day after appealing to soldiers to stop killing.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Around 75,000 killed; a fifth of the population left, most to the United States.

events.title: The Chapultepec Accords
events.what: Ended the war and turned the FMLN guerrillas into a political party.

culture.label: Pupusas
culture.text: Stuffed corn flatbreads with curtido — the national dish, with its own national day.

culture.label: Surfing
culture.text: El Tunco and Punta Roca have some of the best right-hand point breaks in the Americas.

culture.label: Landscape
culture.text: The Land of Volcanoes: over twenty of them in a country the size of Wales.

culture.label: La Palma
culture.text: Fernando Llort's naïf style turned a whole town into an artisan centre.

culture.label: Diaspora
culture.text: Roughly a quarter of Salvadorans live abroad, and remittances are a fifth of the economy.

talkAbout: Pupusas — and whether rice or corn dough is better.
Surfing and the Pacific coast.
Family in the United States; nearly everyone has some.
avoid: The civil war and its massacres are within living memory. Gangs and the current security crackdown divide people sharply.

people.name: George Cadle Price
people.why: Led Belize to independence in 1981 and is called the father of the nation.

people.name: Andy Palacio
people.why: His album Wátina brought Garífuna music to the world just before he died at 47.

people.name: Zee Edgell
people.why: Beka Lamb was the first widely read Belizean novel and is taught across the Caribbean.

people.name: Antonio Soberanis Gómez
people.why: Led the 1930s workers' movement that began the road to self-government.

people.name: Marion Jones
people.why: An early campaigner for Belizean self-rule and constitutional reform.

events.title: The Baymen
events.what: English logwood cutters settled the coast, in territory Spain claimed but never controlled.

events.title: The Battle of St. George's Caye
events.what: Baymen and freed slaves repelled a Spanish fleet; the anniversary is a national holiday.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Belize left British rule, the last mainland American colony to do so.

events.title: The blue bond
events.what: Belize restructured its debt in exchange for protecting a large share of its ocean — a model since copied.

culture.label: Reef
culture.text: The Belize Barrier Reef and the Great Blue Hole, both World Heritage-listed.

culture.label: Garífuna
culture.text: Punta rock and Settlement Day on 19 November, when drums come out across the south.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: English is official, Kriol is the common tongue, and Spanish, Maya, Garifuna, Mandarin and Plautdietsch are all spoken.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Rice and beans with stewed chicken, and hudut — fish in coconut broth with mashed plantain.

culture.label: Both worlds
culture.text: Central American by geography, Caribbean by culture, and a member of CARICOM.

talkAbout: The reef and the Blue Hole.
Garífuna music and Settlement Day.
How many languages get used in a single conversation.
avoid: Guatemala's territorial claim to Belize is a serious national concern, now before the International Court of Justice.

people.name: Juan Pablo Duarte
people.why: Founded the secret society that won independence from Haiti in 1844.

people.name: Oscar de la Renta
people.why: Dressed first ladies and film stars for fifty years from a house he built himself.

people.name: The Mirabal sisters
people.why: Murdered by Trujillo's regime; the UN made the date of their deaths the day against violence towards women.

people.name: Juan Luis Guerra
people.why: Took merengue and bachata worldwide and has won more than twenty Grammys.

people.name: Pedro Martínez
people.why: Three Cy Young Awards and one of the greatest pitching peaks in the sport's history.

events.title: Santo Domingo founded
events.what: The oldest continuously inhabited European city in the Americas, and the base for the whole conquest.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The Dominican Republic broke away from Haiti, which had ruled the whole island for 22 years.

events.title: The Trujillo dictatorship
events.what: Thirty-one years of one man's rule, including the 1937 massacre of Haitians at the border.

events.title: Trujillo assassinated
events.what: His killing opened the way to democracy, via civil war and a US intervention in 1965.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Merengue and bachata both come from here, and both are danced socially by everyone.

culture.label: Baseball
culture.text: More major leaguers per head than anywhere; San Pedro de Macorís alone has produced dozens.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: La bandera — rice, beans and meat — every lunchtime; mangú for breakfast.

culture.label: Geography
culture.text: The Caribbean's highest peak and its lowest point are both in this one country.

culture.label: Carnival
culture.text: February carnival, with the horned diablo cojuelo masks of La Vega.

talkAbout: Baseball, and which players come from their town.
Merengue and bachata.
Food, especially mangú and sancocho.
avoid: Relations with Haiti, and the status of Dominicans of Haitian descent, are a difficult and often bitter subject.

people.name: Toussaint Louverture
people.why: Led the only successful slave revolution in history; died in a French prison before it concluded.

people.name: Jean-Jacques Dessalines
people.why: Declared Haiti independent in 1804 and tore the white band from the French flag to make Haiti's.

people.name: Jacques Roumain
people.why: Masters of the Dew is the great Haitian novel and has been translated worldwide.

people.name: Hector Hyppolite
people.why: A Vodou priest whose paintings launched Haitian art onto the world stage.

people.name: Edwidge Danticat
people.why: The most widely read Haitian author in English, writing from and about the diaspora.

events.title: Bois Caïman
events.what: A Vodou ceremony is remembered as the start of the uprising that became the revolution.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Haiti became the first Black republic and the second independent country in the Americas.

events.title: The indemnity
events.what: France demanded payment for its lost 'property' at gunpoint; Haiti paid for 122 years.

events.title: The earthquake
events.what: A magnitude 7.0 quake near Port-au-Prince killed well over 200,000 people.

culture.label: Art
culture.text: Haitian painting and metal sculpture, especially from Croix-des-Bouquets, are collected worldwide.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Kompa is the national dance music; rara bands parade through the streets at Easter.

culture.label: Vodou
culture.text: An officially recognised religion with a full theology, not the horror-film version.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Griot with pikliz, and soup joumou — pumpkin soup eaten every 1 January to mark independence.

culture.label: Kreyòl
culture.text: Haitian Creole is spoken by everyone and is co-official with French.

talkAbout: The revolution — it is the founding pride of the country and rarely taught properly abroad.
Art and music.
Soup joumou and what it commemorates.
avoid: 'Poorest country in the hemisphere' framings are resented; the reasons are historical and external as much as internal. Vodou is a religion, not a curiosity.

people.name: Lynden Pindling
people.why: Led the Bahamas to majority rule and independence, and is called the father of the nation.

people.name: Sidney Poitier
people.why: Bahamian-raised, and the first Black man to win the Academy Award for Best Actor.

people.name: Pauline Davis-Thompson
people.why: Olympic champion and part of the 'Golden Girls' relay team of 2000.

people.name: Amos Ferguson
people.why: A house painter whose religious folk art on cardboard hangs in major museums.

people.name: Dame Doris Johnson
people.why: Led the campaign for women's suffrage and became the first woman in the Bahamian cabinet.

events.title: First landfall
events.what: Columbus's first landing in the Americas was on a Bahamian island, probably San Salvador.

events.title: The pirate republic
events.what: Nassau was a pirate base until the Crown reasserted control; Blackbeard operated from here.

events.title: Majority rule
events.what: The Black majority won government for the first time, a date still marked as a public holiday.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The Bahamas left British rule after 250 years as a colony.

culture.label: Junkanoo
culture.text: A street parade at Boxing Day and New Year with costumes built over months and cowbell-driven rhythm.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Conch — cracked, in salad or in fritters — is the national food, plus rock lobster and guava duff.

culture.label: Sailing
culture.text: The Bahamian sloop is the national boat, and regattas are serious island events.

culture.label: Geography
culture.text: Around 700 islands and 2,400 cays; roughly thirty are inhabited.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: Athletics and basketball produce a steady stream of internationals for a country of 400,000.

talkAbout: Junkanoo, and which shack they support.
Which island or 'Family Island' their people are from.
Sailing and regattas.
avoid: The Bahamas is not Jamaica or the wider Caribbean lumped together. Hurricane Dorian in 2019 devastated Abaco and Grand Bahama and is still raw.

people.name: Eric Williams
people.why: Capitalism and Slavery reshaped how the slave trade is understood; he then led the country for 25 years.

people.name: V. S. Naipaul
people.why: Nobel laureate in 2001, whose A House for Mr Biswas draws on Indo-Trinidadian life.

people.name: C. L. R. James
people.why: The Black Jacobins and Beyond a Boundary are landmarks in history and in sports writing.

people.name: Brian Lara
people.why: Holds the highest individual score in both Test and first-class cricket.

people.name: Mighty Sparrow
people.why: The Calypso King of the World, and the genre's most enduring voice.

events.title: Indentured arrival
events.what: The Fatel Razack brought the first Indian indentured workers; their descendants are now the largest group.

events.title: The steelpan invented
events.what: Musicians in Port of Spain hammered oil drums into tuned instruments — the only acoustic instrument invented in the twentieth century.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Trinidad and Tobago left British rule, becoming a republic in 1976.

events.title: The Black Power revolution
events.what: Mass protests and an army mutiny forced deep changes to the country's politics and economy.

culture.label: Steelpan
culture.text: The national instrument, invented here; Panorama pits huge steel orchestras against each other at Carnival.

culture.label: Carnival
culture.text: Two days of mas before Lent, starting with J'ouvert in mud and paint before dawn.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Calypso, soca and chutney soca, the last blending Indian and Caribbean traditions.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Doubles for breakfast, roti, bake and shark, and pelau — Indian, African and Creole on one island.

culture.label: Economy
culture.text: Oil and gas rather than tourism, which makes it unlike most of its neighbours.

talkAbout: Carnival, and whether they play mas.
Steelpan and Panorama.
Doubles, and where to get the best.
avoid: Politics tends to split along African and Indian lines and is a sore subject. Don't call Tobago an afterthought — Tobagonians notice.

people.name: Vere Bird
people.why: Trade unionist who led Antigua to independence and dominated its politics for decades.

people.name: Viv Richards
people.why: The most intimidating batsman of his era, who never wore a helmet.

people.name: Jamaica Kincaid
people.why: A Small Place is a furious, brilliant essay on tourism and colonialism in her home island.

people.name: Andy Roberts
people.why: The first Antiguan to play for the West Indies and the spearhead of its great fast-bowling era.

people.name: King Short Shirt
people.why: 'Nobody Go Run Me' became an anthem of Antiguan self-assertion.

events.title: English settlement
events.what: Antigua became a sugar colony worked by enslaved Africans, whose descendants are most of the population.

events.title: Nelson's Dockyard
events.what: Horatio Nelson was based here; the dockyard is the only working Georgian naval yard left anywhere.

events.title: Immediate emancipation
events.what: Antigua freed its enslaved people outright, skipping the 'apprenticeship' most colonies imposed.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Antigua and Barbuda left British rule.

culture.label: Beaches
culture.text: 365 of them, the tourist board insists — one for every day of the year.

culture.label: Cricket
culture.text: The old Antigua Recreation Ground saw both of Brian Lara's world-record scores.

culture.label: Sailing
culture.text: Antigua Sailing Week draws crews from across the Atlantic every spring.

culture.label: Carnival
culture.text: Held in August to mark emancipation rather than before Lent.

culture.label: Barbuda
culture.text: Land on Barbuda is held communally by its residents — unusual anywhere, and fiercely defended.

talkAbout: Cricket, and the West Indies.
Sailing week and the dockyard.
The difference between Antigua and Barbuda, which matters to Barbudans.
avoid: Hurricane Irma made Barbuda uninhabitable in 2017 and the fight over its communal land since is bitter.

people.name: Errol Barrow
people.why: Led Barbados to independence in 1966 and built its free education system.

people.name: Rihanna
people.why: One of the best-selling artists ever, and a Barbadian National Hero at 33.

people.name: Garfield Sobers
people.why: Widely considered the greatest all-rounder the game has produced.

people.name: Bussa
people.why: Led the largest slave revolt in Barbadian history; his statue stands at a main roundabout.

people.name: George Lamming
people.why: In the Castle of My Skin is a founding text of Caribbean literature.

events.title: English settlement
events.what: Barbados became the model sugar colony, and its slave code was copied across the English Caribbean.

events.title: Bussa's rebellion
events.what: Thousands rose against slavery; it was crushed but fed the abolition campaign in Britain.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Barbados left British rule after 339 years.

events.title: Becoming a republic
events.what: Barbados removed the British monarch as head of state and installed its own president.

culture.label: Rum
culture.text: Rum was invented here; Mount Gay has been distilling since 1703 and rum shops are the social centre of every village.

culture.label: Cricket
culture.text: Kensington Oval is a place of pilgrimage, and Barbados has produced West Indies greats out of all proportion.

culture.label: Crop Over
culture.text: A harvest festival turned into a summer carnival, ending in Grand Kadooment.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Flying fish and cou-cou is the national dish; Oistins on a Friday night is a fish fry the whole island attends.

culture.label: Bajan
culture.text: Bajan dialect is quick and dry, and the humour with it is a national characteristic.

talkAbout: Cricket, and the great West Indies teams.
Rum, and which distillery they prefer.
Crop Over and Oistins.
avoid: 'Little England' is an old nickname many now dislike. Slavery's legacy and reparations are actively debated here, seriously.

people.name: Eugenia Charles
people.why: The Caribbean's first woman prime minister, in office fifteen years and nicknamed the Iron Lady.

people.name: Jean Rhys
people.why: Wide Sargasso Sea reimagined Jane Eyre from the Creole wife's side; she was born in Roseau.

people.name: Ophelia Marie
people.why: The Lady of Song, who made cadence-lypso a Dominican export.

people.name: Rosie Douglas
people.why: A Black Power activist deported from Canada who returned to lead his country.

people.name: Chief Charles Williams
people.why: Long-serving chief of the Kalinago Territory, and a defender of Indigenous land rights.

events.title: Kalinago resistance
events.what: Kalinago defence kept Europeans off the island for 250 years longer than its neighbours.

events.title: The Carib Reserve
events.what: Britain set aside land that is now the Kalinago Territory, the last Indigenous Caribbean territory.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Dominica left British rule, then survived a hurricane and two coup attempts in its first years.

events.title: Hurricane Maria
events.what: Destroyed most of the island's buildings and crops; Dominica set out to become the first climate-resilient nation.

culture.label: Nature Isle
culture.text: Boiling Lake, 365 rivers and rainforest — the least developed and most mountainous of the Lesser Antilles.

culture.label: Kalinago
culture.text: The only Caribbean island with a substantial surviving Indigenous population and territory.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Bouyon and cadence-lypso, both born here, plus a strong Creole music festival.

culture.label: Kwéyòl
culture.text: An Antillean Creole is widely spoken alongside English, a legacy of French settlement.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Callaloo soup, mountain chicken (a frog, now protected), and river crayfish.

talkAbout: Hiking, the Waitukubuli trail and the Boiling Lake.
Kalinago culture and the territory.
Creole language and the World Creole Music Festival.
avoid: Don't confuse Dominica with the Dominican Republic — it happens constantly and irritates. Maria's damage is recent and personal.

people.name: Maurice Bishop
people.why: Led the 1979 revolution and was executed by his own comrades four years later.

people.name: Kirani James
people.why: Won the 400 m at London 2012 — Grenada's first Olympic medal, and it was gold.

people.name: Eric Gairy
people.why: Led Grenada to independence, and was known at the UN for his campaign on unidentified flying objects.

people.name: Julien Fédon
people.why: Led a near-successful revolt against British rule inspired by the French and Haitian revolutions.

people.name: Jean Augustine
people.why: Grenada-born, the first Black woman elected to Canada's parliament and to its cabinet.

events.title: Fédon's rebellion
events.what: A revolt of free coloureds and enslaved people nearly took the island from Britain.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Grenada left British rule, the smallest independent country in the western hemisphere at the time.

events.title: The revolution
events.what: The New Jewel Movement took power bloodlessly and aligned with Cuba.

events.title: The US invasion
events.what: After Bishop's execution, American forces invaded and removed the government.

culture.label: Nutmeg
culture.text: The Isle of Spice: nutmeg and mace appear on the flag, and Grenada was long the world's second producer.

culture.label: Carnival
culture.text: Spicemas in August, with Jab Jab devils covered in oil and molasses at J'ouvert.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Oil down — breadfruit, salt meat and callaloo in coconut milk — cooked in one pot for a crowd.

culture.label: Underwater sculpture
culture.text: The world's first underwater sculpture park sits in Molinere Bay.

culture.label: Three islands
culture.text: Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique, each with distinct traditions.

talkAbout: Spices, and how nutmeg is processed.
Kirani James and the 2012 Olympics.
Spicemas and Jab Jab.
avoid: The revolution, Bishop's killing and the 1983 invasion still divide families; his remains were never found.

people.name: Robert Bradshaw
people.why: Trade union leader and the dominant figure in the islands' move to self-government.

people.name: Kim Collins
people.why: World 100 m champion in 2003, from a country of fewer than 50,000 people.

people.name: Simeon Daniel
people.why: Nevis's first premier and the architect of its autonomy within the federation.

people.name: Caryl Phillips
people.why: St Kitts-born, one of the leading novelists of the Caribbean diaspora in Britain.

people.name: Alexander Hamilton
people.why: Born on Nevis; built the American financial system and is now a musical.

events.title: The mother colony
events.what: St Kitts was the first English Caribbean colony, and the base for settling several others.

events.title: Brimstone Hill
events.what: Enslaved labourers built a fortress called the Gibraltar of the West Indies, now World Heritage-listed.

events.title: Independence
events.what: St Kitts and Nevis became the newest sovereign state in the Americas, and remains the smallest.

events.title: The end of sugar
events.what: After 350 years, the sugar industry closed, and the economy turned to tourism and citizenship sales.

culture.label: Sugar train
culture.text: The old cane railway now circles the island as a scenic line.

culture.label: Carnival
culture.text: Sugar Mas runs from Christmas into January, with masquerade troupes and Big Drum.

culture.label: Brimstone Hill
culture.text: A hilltop fortress with a view of four other islands on a clear day.

culture.label: Monkeys
culture.text: Green vervet monkeys, brought from Africa in the 1600s, now outnumber the people.

culture.label: Two islands
culture.text: Nevis has its own assembly and a standing right to secede, narrowly rejected in 1998.

talkAbout: Sugar Mas and masquerade traditions.
Brimstone Hill and the island's forts.
Kim Collins and athletics.
avoid: The Nevis secession question is live politics. Citizenship-by-investment gets criticised abroad and locals are tired of it.

people.name: Derek Walcott
people.why: Nobel laureate in 1992, whose Omeros transplants Homer to a St Lucian fishing village.

people.name: Arthur Lewis
people.why: The first Black person to win a Nobel in a field other than peace, for development economics.

people.name: John Compton
people.why: Led St Lucia to independence and served as prime minister across four decades.

people.name: Julien Alfred
people.why: Won the Olympic 100 m in 2024 — St Lucia's first Olympic medal of any colour.

people.name: Dunstan St Omer
people.why: Designed the national flag and painted the altarpieces in churches across the island.

events.title: Fourteen changes of hands
events.what: Britain and France fought over the island so often it was called the Helen of the West Indies.

events.title: Independence
events.what: St Lucia left British rule.

events.title: Two Nobel Prizes
events.what: Lewis and Walcott gave the island more Nobel laureates per head than anywhere on earth.

events.title: The Pitons listed
events.what: The two volcanic spires above Soufrière became a World Heritage site.

culture.label: The Pitons
culture.text: Gros and Petit Piton rise straight out of the sea and are on the flag, the beer and everything else.

culture.label: Kwéyòl
culture.text: French-based Creole is widely spoken; Jounen Kwéyòl in October celebrates it.

culture.label: Jazz
culture.text: The St Lucia Jazz Festival has drawn international acts since 1992.

culture.label: Flower societies
culture.text: La Rose and La Marguerite are rival festival societies that split villages good-naturedly.

culture.label: Bananas
culture.text: Bananas were the backbone of the economy until EU trade rules changed in the 1990s.

talkAbout: Walcott and the two Nobel Prizes.
Creole language and Jounen Kwéyòl.
The Pitons and the drive-in volcano.
avoid: St Lucians are proud of Kwéyòl; don't call it broken French. The loss of the banana trade caused real hardship.

people.name: Joseph Chatoyer
people.why: Led resistance to the British and is the country's only national hero.

people.name: Ralph Gonsalves
people.why: In office since 2001 and one of the Caribbean's most prominent voices on reparations.

people.name: Milton Cato
people.why: Led the country to independence in 1979.

people.name: Kevin Lyttle
people.why: 'Turn Me On' became an international soca hit and the country's best-known song.

people.name: Pamenos Ballantyne
people.why: Won the Trinidad marathon a record number of times and carried the flag at three Olympics.

events.title: The Garifuna
events.what: Shipwrecked Africans and Kalinago intermarried; the British deported the survivors to Central America.

events.title: La Soufrière erupts
events.what: An eruption killed around 1,600 people, hours before Mount Pelée destroyed Saint-Pierre on Martinique.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines left British rule, weeks after a volcanic eruption.

events.title: La Soufrière again
events.what: Explosive eruptions covered the island in ash and forced 20,000 people from their homes.

culture.label: Grenadines
culture.text: Bequia, Mustique and Tobago Cays make this one of the great sailing grounds in the world.

culture.label: Vincy Mas
culture.text: Carnival in late June and early July, ending with J'ouvert and Mardi Gras.

culture.label: La Soufrière
culture.text: An active volcano at the north of the main island, climbed by visitors and watched by everyone.

culture.label: Breadfruit
culture.text: Bligh brought breadfruit here on the Bounty's second voyage; the original tree's descendants still grow.

culture.label: Bequia
culture.text: One of the few places still permitted a small traditional whale hunt under IWC rules.

talkAbout: Sailing the Grenadines.
Vincy Mas, and whether June carnival beats a pre-Lent one.
Breadfruit, and the Bounty story.
avoid: The 2021 eruption displaced a fifth of the country. Traditional whaling on Bequia is contested and easily misread by outsiders.
